statement: Capturing the training step as a CUDA graph (torch.compile mode="reduce-overhead") raises num_steps and lowers val_bpb in the frozen 300s H200 v2c scope, by removing per-launch CPU dispatch across the ~572 kernel launches each step issues.
rationale: The profile shows the GPU idle ~43% of wall while issuing ~572 launches per optimizer step, most of them small: 32,071 elementwise launches account for only 8.1% of kernel time. That is the signature of a dispatch-bound loop, which is exactly what graph capture removes. It is the cheapest test of the gap mediator because it is a compile flag rather than a kernel rewrite, so a null result cleanly indicts the mediator rather than the implementation.

prediction.statement: Candidate val_bpb is below its frozen same-GPU control by more than the gate, with num_steps and mfu_percent both strictly higher than the control's.

falsifiers: The paired delta does not clear the gate.
num_steps does not rise, which refutes graph capture as a way to reach the gap mediator.
num_steps rises but val_bpb does not fall, contradicting the token law.
The arm dies or produces a graph-capture error, which is an implementation null and not evidence about the mechanism.

intervention.summary: Change the torch.compile call in train.py to mode="reduce-overhead" so the step is captured as a CUDA graph. Note the prior-campaign warning that plain max-autotune segfaulted via CUDA graphs on a different stack; if capture fails, fall back to max-autotune-no-cudagraphs and record the failure as an implementation null.
